llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions are internally consistent with a constraint-aware fitness planner and do not request unrelated credentials or system access; the only notable item is an in-doc install command pointing at a GitHub repo (the skill itself does not auto-install anything).

dimensions.detail: Name, description, required inputs, and the provided elicitation/record/execution prompts all align with a profile-first fitness planning skill. The skill does not request unrelated binaries, environment variables, or config paths.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the prompt files instruct the agent to elicit user fitness data and produce structured outputs (e.g., PrimaryDecision, MissingInputs). They do not tell the agent to read system files, access credentials, or transmit data to external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This package is instruction-only and has no install spec in the registry metadata (lowest-risk). However, the SKILL.md (and README/other docs) include a recommended install command that would pull code from https://github.com/sirsws/akm via `npx skills add ...`. That command is not executed by the platform automatically, but if a user runs it it will download code from an external GitHub repository — review that repository before running the command.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths are required. The skill does not request sensitive tokens or unrelated service access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags show default behavior (always:false, agent-invocable allowed). The skill does not request permanent presence nor modify other skills or system-wide configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and focused on eliciting a fitness profile and producing constrained workout decisions. Things to consider before installing or running it: 1) The skill file includes an example install command that pulls a repository from GitHub (https://github.com/sirsws/akm). The registry entry itself has no install script, so the platform won't auto-run that — but if you run the npx command yourself, review the referenced GitHub repo first. 2) The skill explicitly says it is NOT a medical or rehabilitation tool — do not substitute it for professional medical advice. 3) It asks for personal fitness details (injuries, recovery, logs). Be mindful of privacy: avoid sharing identifying medical history unless you are comfortable. 4) Autonomous invocation is allowed by default on the platform (this is normal); if you do not want the agent to call the skill without your prompt, disable autonomous invocation in agent settings. 5) If you plan to run the suggested npx install, inspect the repo and its code for unexpected network calls or scripts before executing.
